title: Cantar de mio Cid
titleEn: The Song of the Cid — The king of Seville repulsed; the uncut beard; a second gift for the king (tiradas 75–77, lines 1221–1286)
part: Tiradas 75–77 · The king of Seville repulsed; the uncut beard; a second gift for the king (lines 1221–1286)
source: Ramón Menéndez Pidal (ed.), Poema de mio Cid, 2.ª edición corregida (Clásicos Castellanos 24; Madrid: Ediciones de “La Lectura”, 1923), pp. 208–212, lines 1221–1286 (tiradas 75–77). Text follows Pidal's critical text exactly, including its old accentuation and mixed spellings; Pidal's italics (his editorial restorations) are shown in [brackets], and a line he restores whole is flagged in its note. Line numbers are Pidal's. Pronunciation convention: reconstructed twelfth-century Castilian. Translations made fresh from the Old Spanish; Pidal's notes and vocabulary (1908–11) the lexical aids.

sentences.t:
Ya folgava mio Çid con todas sus conpañas:
âquel rey de Sevilla el mandado llegava,
que presa es Valençia, que non gela enparan,
vino los ve[e]r con treynta mill de armas.
sentences.l:
Now was-resting my Çid with all his companies:
to-that king of Sevilla the message was-coming,
that taken is Valençia, that not it-from-him they-defend,
he-came them to-see with thirty thousand of arms.
sentences.i: My Çid was at rest now with all his companies. To the king of Seville came the news that Valencia was taken and that no one was holding it against him; he came to attack them with thirty thousand men under arms.
sentences.n: Tirada 75 (assonance á-a) — the king of Seville tries to win back Valencia (Pidal: El Rey de Sevilla quiere recobrar Valencia). Line-ends conpañas, llegava, enparan, armas, batalla, barba … agua, escapa, plata, llegavan; ganançia (v. 1231) counts with them. folgava, imperfect of folgar, 'to rest, take one's ease' (f- for h-: holgar). âquel: so printed by Pidal, with a circumflex, as lâ at v. 914: read here as a + aquel, 'to that (king)', the two a's run together (Pidal gives no note on the form); the news (el mandado) 'came to' him. Pidal's note to v. 1222: from 1091 Seville had no kings of its own, having been conquered by the Almoravids; but rey of the Moors is the usual name for any general or emir (v. 637), and here 'king of Seville' can only mean the Almoravid general who governed Seville. presa, participle of prender, 'taken'. non gela enparan: enparar = amparar, 'to defend, protect'; gela = ge la, 'it … him'. Pidal gives no note here; read as 'they (the Moors) do not hold it against him (the Çid)', but whose 'him' is meant is not certain. Pidal's note to v. 1224: ver, in military language, was the same as 'atacar', 'to attack' (compare v. 1124): vino los ve[e]r, 'he came to attack them'; the second e of ve[e]r is Pidal's. de armas, 'under arms'.

sentences.t:
Aprés de la uerta ovieron la batalla,
arrancólos mio Çid el de la luenga barba.
sentences.l:
Near of the orchard they-had the battle,
routed-them my Çid he of the long beard.
sentences.i: By the orchards they fought the battle, and my Çid of the long beard routed them.
sentences.n: Aprés de, 'near, close by'. uerta = huerta, the irrigated orchard-land round Valencia (spelled here without h). ovieron la batalla, 'they had (fought) the battle' (aver as a full verb). arrancólos = arrancó los, 'he routed them' (arrancar, 'to rout'; arrancada, 'rout, victory'). el de la luenga barba, 'he of the long beard', a standing epithet of the Çid — and the beard becomes the matter of the next tirada (luenga = larga, 'long').

sentences.t:
Fata dentro en Xátiva duró el arrancada,
en el passar de Xúcar i veriédes barata,
moros en a[r]ruenço amidos bever agua.
sentences.l:
As-far-as inside in Xátiva lasted the rout,
in the crossing of Xúcar there you-would-see commotion,
Moors in drift against-their-will to-drink water.
sentences.i: The rout lasted right into Játiva; at the crossing of the Júcar you would have seen a scramble there, Moors floundering against the current, drinking water whether they would or no.
sentences.n: Fata = hasta, 'as far as' (f- for h-). dentro en, 'inside'. el arrancada: el, the old form of the feminine article before a word beginning in a. Xátiva, Xúcar = Játiva and the river Júcar (x = [ʃ]). i, 'there'. veriédes, conditional 2nd pl. of veer, 'you would have seen' — the minstrel speaking to his hearers. barata: Pidal gives no note here; the word is 'a dealing, a bargain', and in a battle it seems to mean 'turmoil, confusion' — the sense is not certain. Pidal's note to v. 1229: 'los moros ronceando (a la ronza contra la corriente) bebían agua sin querer', 'the Moors, drifting (struggling against the current), drank water against their will'. It is frequent in descriptions of battles, he says, to show fugitives gorging on water while crossing a river: in the Poema de Fernán González, 358c, the men of Toulouse, driven against the Ebro, 'bevían mal de su grado', and in the Chanson de Roland, 2473, the Saracens pursued by Charlemagne drown in the Ebro. a[r]ruenço, its first r Pidal's (in italics). amidos, 'unwillingly' (Latin invitus, v. 84). bever, infinitive standing for a finite verb: the line has no conjugated verb.

sentences.t:
Aquel rey de [Sevilla] con tres colpes escapa.
Tornado es mio Çid con toda esta ganançia.
sentences.l:
That king of [Sevilla] with three blows escapes.
Returned is my Çid with all this gain.
sentences.i: That king of Seville gets away with three wounds. My Çid has come back with all this booty.
sentences.n: [Sevilla] is in italics, a word Pidal supplies. con tres colpes, 'with three blows' (colpe = golpe), i.e. wounded three times. escapa, present amid the preterites. Tornado es, ser + participle with a verb of motion, 'has returned'. ganançia, 'gain, booty'.

sentences.t:
Buena f[o] la de Valençia quando ganaron la casa,
mas mucho fue provechosa, sabet, esta arrancada:
a todos los menores cayeron çient marcos de plata.
sentences.l:
Good was the of Valençia when they-won the town,
but more was profitable, know-ye, this rout:
to all the lesser-men fell a-hundred marks of silver.
sentences.i: Good was the winning of Valencia, when they took the city, but this victory, be sure of it, paid better still: to every one of the lesser men fell a hundred marks of silver.
sentences.n: Buena f[o] la de Valençia: f[o] = fue, its o Pidal's (in italics). la de Valençia, 'that of Valencia', a feminine noun understood — apparently ganançia from the line before, or the arrancada of the next; Pidal gives no note, so which is meant is not certain. Pidal's note to v. 1232: la casa, 'la población, la ciudad', 'the town, the city' (compare vv. 62, 1550, 2877). Pidal's note to v. 1233: mas mucho is the comparative of mucho, and so means simply 'más', 'more'; arrancada, 'victoria'. sabet, 'know ye' (= sabed), the minstrel's aside. los menores, 'the lesser men', apparently the rank and file as against the captains (Pidal gives no note here). cayeron, 'fell (to)', as le caen at v. 1217. marcos, 'marks', a weight of silver used as money.

sentences.t: Las nuevas del cavallero ya ve[e]des do llegavan.
sentences.l: The affairs of-the knight now you-see where they-were-reaching.
sentences.i: Now you see how far the fortunes of the knight were reaching.
sentences.n: Pidal's note to v. 1235: Las nuevas, 'los asuntos, los negocios', 'the affairs, the business' — not here 'tidings'. del cavallero, the Çid. veedes = veis, 2nd pl. present of veer, its second e Pidal's (in italics); the minstrel turns to his hearers. do = donde, 'where, how far'; llegavan, imperfect.

sentences.i: Great is the joy among all those Christians with my Çid Ruy Díaz, born in a good hour. His beard is growing now, and grows longer and longer;
sentences.n: Tirada 76 (assonance á-o) — the Çid leaves his beard uncut; the wealth of the Çid's men (Pidal: El Cid deja su barba intonsa.—Riqueza de los del Cid). Line-ends cristianos, nasco, allongando, atanto, echado, tajado … recabdo, vassallos, aguisado; nasco fits with its stressed a and final o. Grand = grande. essos = esos. R[o]y, the o Pidal's (in italics). el que en buen ora nasco, 'he who was born in a good hour', the standing formula (nasco, preterite of nascer). Yal = ya le, 'now … to him'. vale allongando = va le alongando, 'it goes on lengthening for him': ir + gerund, with le run onto the verb (allongar = alargar, 'to lengthen'). The beard is the Çid's standing mark (el de la luenga barba, v. 1226).

sentences.t:
ca dixera mio Çid de la su boca atanto:
“por amor de rey Alffonsso, que de tierra me a echado”
nin entrarié en ella tigera, ni un pelo non avrié tajado,
e que fablassen desto moros e cristianos.
sentences.l:
for had-said my Çid from the his mouth this-much:
“for love of king Alffonsso, who from land me has cast-out”
nor would-enter in it scissors, nor a hair not would-have cut,
and that might-speak of-this Moors and Christians.
sentences.i: for my Çid had said this much with his own mouth: “For the love of King Alfonso, who has cast me out of the land” — no scissors should come into it, nor a single hair be cut, and Moors and Christians alike should talk of it.
sentences.n: The beard vow. ca, 'for'. dixera, the -ra form as a pluperfect indicative, 'had said'. de la su boca, article + possessive, 'from his own mouth'. atanto, 'so much, this much'. Pidal's closing quotation mark stands after echado: only v. 1240 is given as the Çid's own words, and the vow itself runs on in reported speech, with conditionals (entrarié, 'would enter'; avrié tajado, conditional perfect, 'would have cut') and an imperfect subjunctive (fablassen, 'that they should speak', f- for h-). me a echado, 'has cast me out' (a = ha); de tierra, 'out of the land', the stock phrase for exile. tigera = tijera, 'scissors'. nin … ni … non, the double negative. Pidal's note to v. 1241: compare v. 2059. Not cutting the beard or the hair, and at times not even the nails, was a sign of grief, often kept after an oath or promise, as the Çid does here; even in times when a shaven beard was the fashion, it was let grow during mourning — so the Catholic King, usually clean-shaven, wore a beard after the death of Prince Don Juan. Pidal's note to v. 1242: moros e cristianos, 'todo el mundo, todos', 'everyone' (compare v. 145). desto = de esto.

sentences.t:
Mio Çid don Rodrigo en Valençia está folgando.
con él Minaya Álbar Fáñez que nos le parte de so braço.
sentences.l:
My Çid don Rodrigo in Valençia is resting.
with him Minaya Álbar Fáñez who not-himself from-him parts from his arm.
sentences.i: My Çid, Don Rodrigo, is taking his ease in Valencia, and with him Minaya Álvar Fáñez, who never leaves his side.
sentences.n: está folgando, estar + gerund, 'is resting' (folgar, v. 1221). The full stop after folgando and the small c of con are Pidal's. nos le parte = no se le parte, 'does not part from him' (partirse de, 'to go away from'); de so braço, 'from his arm', i.e. from his side (so = su).

sentences.t:
Los que exieron de tierra de ritad son abondados,
a todos les dio en Valençia [el Campeador contado]
casas y heredades de que son pagados;
el amor de mio Çid ya lo ivan provando.
sentences.l:
Those who went-out from land of wealth are abounding,
to all to-them gave in Valençia [the Campeador renowned]
houses and estates of which they-are satisfied;
the love of my Çid now it they-were proving.
sentences.i: Those who went out into exile with him are rich in wealth: to every one of them in Valencia the renowned Campeador gave houses and estates, with which they are well content; the Çid's love they were tasting now in deed.
sentences.n: Pidal's note to v. 1245: here those who went into exile with the Cid are set against those who joined his army later, v. 1248 (compare vv. 917, 1199); in the same way los que son aquí (v. 1258) are set against mios vasallos (v. 1261). The sharing-out of the city is made in favour of the old vassals (p. 99); the newcomers (allegadizos) share only in the booty. exieron, preterite of exir, 'went out' (= salieron); exir de tierra, to go into exile. de ritad son abondados, 'are abounding in wealth': ritad: Pidal gives no note here; most likely a noun made on rico, 'riches' (as rictad, v. 688, which Pidal glosses 'riqueza'; rritad, v. 1189); abondados, 'well supplied, abounding' (= abundantes) — the second vowel is broken on the scan and is read as o. The second half of v. 1246, el Campeador contado, is in italics: Pidal's restoration. contado, 'renowned, esteemed', the standing epithet of the Campeador (literally 'counted, reckoned'). heredades, 'estates, landed property'. y, so printed, where the poem usually has e. son pagados, 'are satisfied' (pagarse de, 'to be pleased with'), not 'paid'. ivan provando, ir + gerund, 'they were coming to prove', i.e. to know by experience.

sentences.i: Those who came later are all content too; but my Çid sees that, with the riches they had taken, they would gladly go off home if they could.
sentences.n: Los que f[o]ron después, 'those who were (with him) afterwards', the later recruits of Pidal's note to v. 1245; f[o]ron = fueron, its o Pidal's (in italics). veelo = vee lo, 'sees it', present of veer (= ve). avién tomados, 'they had taken', the participle agreeing with averes. que … que: the que is said again after the clause that comes between. sis = si se: si se pudiessen ir, 'if they could get away' (pudiessen, imperfect subjunctive of poder). fer lo ien = lo farían, the split conditional: the infinitive fer (= fazer, 'to do'), then the pronoun, then ien (from avién). de grado, 'willingly'.

sentences.t:
Esto mandó mio Çid, Minaya lo ovo conssejado:
que ningún omne de los sos [que con él ganaron algo]
ques le non spidiés, o nol besás la mano,
sentences.l:
This ordered my Çid, Minaya it had counselled:
that no man of the his [who with him won something]
who-himself from-him not should-take-leave, or not-to-him should-kiss the hand,
sentences.i: This my Çid commanded, and Minaya had advised it: that any man of his own, who had won wealth with him, who left without taking leave of him or kissing his hand,
sentences.n: mandó, 'commanded'. ovo conssejado, aver + participle, 'had advised' (the past anterior). ningún omne de los sos, 'no man of his (men)'; omne = hombre; sos = sus. The second half of v. 1252, que con él ganaron algo, is in italics: Pidal's restoration. algo, 'something of value, wealth'. ques le non spidiés = que se le non espidiesse, 'who should not take leave of him': ques = que + se, with le and the negative still ahead of the verb; spidiés, imperfect subjunctive of espedirse (despedirse), espidiesse with its final -e lost (-sse > -s), as curiás, v. 329. nol besás = no le besasse, 'should not kiss his hand' (nol, no + le; besás, imperfect subjunctive, cut like spidiés). Pidal's note to v. 1252b: the vassal could not leave his lord without taking leave of him and saying, 'despídome de vos et bésovos la mano, et de aquí adelante non so vuestro vasallo', 'I take leave of you and kiss your hand, and from now on I am not your vassal.' The sentence runs on into the next lines.

sentences.t:
sil pudiessen prender o f[o]sse alcançado,
tomássenle el aver e pusiéssenle en un palo.
sentences.l:
if-him they-could seize or he-were overtaken,
let-them-take-from-him the wealth and let-them-put-him on a stake.
sentences.i: if they could lay hands on him, or he were overtaken, should have his wealth taken from him and be hung up on a gallows.
sentences.n: sil = si le, 'if … him'. prender, 'to take, seize'. f[o]sse alcançado = fuesse alcanzado, 'were overtaken'; the o is Pidal's (in italics). tomássenle, pusiéssenle = tomassen le, pusiessen le: imperfect subjunctives with le run on, 'that they should take from him … put him', the command reported. el aver, 'the wealth' (aver as a noun). Pidal's note to v. 1254: palo, 'horca', 'gallows'.

sentences.t:
Afevos todo aquesto puesto en buen recabdo;
con Minaya Álbar Fáñez él se va conseja[ndo]:
sentences.l:
Behold-you all this put in good order;
with Minaya Álbar Fáñez he himself goes counselling:
sentences.i: See, all this is put in good order; and with Minaya Álvar Fáñez he takes counsel:
sentences.n: Afevos, 'behold', the minstrel's pointing word (afé + vos, v. 262). aquesto = esto. en buen recabdo, 'in good order, safely arranged' (recabdo, 'care, strict order', v. 24). él se va conseja[ndo], 'he goes taking counsel', ir + gerund; the -ndo is Pidal's (in italics).

sentences.i: “If you are willing, Minaya, I wish to have a reckoning of those who are here and have won wealth with me; I will set them down in writing, and let them all be counted,
sentences.n: si vos quisiéredes, future subjunctive of querer after si, the courteous 'if you will'. saber recabdo, 'to know the account, have a reckoning' (recabdo, here 'reckoning'). los que son aquí, 'those who are here': Pidal's note to v. 1245 sets them against mios vasallos (v. 1261), so presumably the later recruits. comigo, 'with me'. meterlos he = los meteré, the split future (the infinitive, the pronoun, then he), 'I will put them'. en escripto, 'in writing'. sean contados, present subjunctive, 'let them be counted'.

sentences.t:
que si algunos furtare o menos le fallar[o],
el aver me avrá a tornar, âquestos myos vassallos
que curian a Valençia e andan arrobdando.”
sentences.l:
that if anyone should-steal or missing him I-should-find,
the wealth to-me he-will-have to return, to-these my vassals
who guard Valençia and go patrolling.”
sentences.i: so that if any man steals away, or I find him missing, he shall have to give his wealth back to me, to these my vassals who guard Valencia and ride the rounds.”
sentences.n: furtare, future subjunctive of furtar (= hurtar, 'to steal'; f- for h-), with algunos, 'any one', and a singular verb. Pidal gives no note on it; with no object it is read here as 'steal away, slip off', but it could mean 'steal' outright; the sense is not certain. menos le fallar[o]: Pidal's note to v. 1260: fallaro, see the note to v. 825; 'si le hallare menos', 'si le echare de menos', 'if I find him missing, if I miss him' (compare v. 798). fallar[o] is the future subjunctive, first person, of fallar (= hallar), with the old -o ending; the o is Pidal's (in italics), and the á-o assonance calls for it. el aver me avrá a tornar, 'he will have to give the wealth back to me': aver a + infinitive, 'to have to', in the future (avrá). âquestos: so printed by Pidal, with a circumflex, as âquel at v. 1222: read here as a + aquestos, 'to these (my vassals)'; Pidal gives no note on the form, so the analysis is offered with caution. myos, with y, as printed. These are presumably the old vassals of Pidal's note to v. 1245. curian, present 3rd pl. of curiar, 'to guard, take care of' (curiás, v. 329). Pidal's note to v. 1261b: arrobdar, 'rondar, hacer el servicio de guardia exterior en una fortaleza', 'to go the rounds, to keep the outer watch of a fortress'; andan arrobdando, andar + gerund.

sentences.t: Allí dixo Minaya: “consejo es aguisado.”
sentences.l: There said Minaya: “counsel it-is fitting.”
sentences.i: Then Minaya said: “That is sound counsel.”
sentences.n: Allí, 'there, thereupon'. aguisado, 'fitting, well judged' (aguisar, from guisa, v. 131).

sentences.i: He ordered them to come to the court and had them all gathered together; when he had them before him, he had them called over by count: three thousand six hundred men had my Çid of Vivar.
sentences.n: Tirada 77 (assonance á) — the muster of the Çid's men; he arranges a new gift for the king (Pidal: Recuento de la gente del Cid.—Este dispone nuevo presente para el rey). Line-ends juntar, nonbrar, Bivar, sonrrisar, adelant, pesar, natural, acá, levar, rogad, sacar, vernán, ganar, voluntad, adobar, abbat; the á-e endings (madre, heredades, naturales, mensage, iffantes, Fáñez) count with them, the unstressed final e being disregarded. Mandólos = mandó los, 'ordered them'. corth = corte, 'court', so spelled; Pidal gives no note. a todos los juntar, the pronoun before the infinitive. falló = halló (f- for h-). por cuenta, 'by count'. fízolos nonbrar, fazer + infinitive, 'he had them named' (nonbrar = nombrar). avie = había, 'he had', without an accent, as printed. el de Bivar, 'he of Vivar'.

sentences.t:
alégrasle el coraçón e tornós a sonrrisar:
“Grado a Dios, Minaya, e a santa María madre!
sentences.l:
rejoices-itself-to-him the heart and turned-himself to smile:
“Thanks to God, Minaya, and to holy Mary mother!
sentences.i: His heart was glad within him and he broke into a smile: “Thanks be to God, Minaya, and to holy Mary, His mother!
sentences.n: alégrasle = alegra se le, 'his heart rejoices' (le, 'to him': the heart is his). tornós = tornó se: tornarse a + infinitive, 'to turn to, begin to'. sonrrisar = sonreír, 'to smile', spelled with rr. Grado a Dios, 'thanks (be) to God' (grado, 'gratitude'). santa María madre, 'holy Mary (His) mother', as at v. 333.

sentences.t:
Con más pocos ixiemos de la casa de Bivar.
Agora avemos riquiza, más avremos adelant.
sentences.l:
With more few we-went-out from the town of Bivar.
Now we-have riches, more we-shall-have forward.
sentences.i: With fewer than these we went out from the town of Vivar. Now we have riches, and more we shall have hereafter.
sentences.n: Pidal's note to v. 1268: más pocos, 'menos', 'fewer' (compare más mucho, v. 1233); casa, 'población, lugar', 'town, place'. ixiemos, preterite 1st pl. of exir, 'we went out' (= salimos). Agora = ahora. riquiza = riqueza. avremos = habremos, future of aver. adelant, 'hereafter, from now on'.

sentences.i: If it please you, Minaya, and you do not take it ill, I wish to send you to Castile, where we have our estates, to King Alfonso, my natural lord;
sentences.n: ploguiere, future subjunctive of plazer, 'should please'. non vos caya en pesar, 'let it not fall on you as a grief', i.e. do not take it amiss (caya, present subjunctive of caer). enbiar vos quiero = quiero enviaros, the pronoun between infinitive and verb. Castiella = Castilla. do = donde. heredades, 'estates, lands held by inheritance'. señor natural, 'natural lord', the lord to whom one owes allegiance by birth.

sentences.t:
destas mis ganançias, que avemos fechas acá,
dar le quiero çient cavallos, e vos ídgelos levar;
sentences.l:
of-these my gains, which we-have made here,
give to-him I-want a-hundred horses, and you go-to-him-them to-take;
sentences.i: of these winnings of mine that we have made here I wish to give him a hundred horses, and you are to go and take them to him;
sentences.n: destas = de estas: 'from these gains of mine'. avemos fechas, aver + participle agreeing with ganançias (fechas = hechas, f- for h-). acá, 'here'. dar le quiero = quiero darle. çient = cien. ídgelos = id + ge + los, 'go … them to him': the imperative id, then ge ('to him', ancestor of modern se) and los, then the infinitive levar (= llevar, 'to carry'): e vos ídgelos levar, 'and do you go and take them to him'.

sentences.t:
desí por mí besalde la mano e firme gelo rogad
por mi mugier [doña Ximena] e mis fijas [naturales],
si f[o]re su merçed quenlas dexe sacar.
sentences.i: then kiss his hand for me, and beg him earnestly, for my wife Doña Ximena and my own daughters, that, if it be his pleasure, he let me take them away.
sentences.n: desí, 'then, after that'. besalde = besadle, imperative + le with d and l swapped (as prestalde, v. 118). firme, 'firmly, earnestly'. gelo rogad, 'beg it of him' (ge lo + imperative rogad). [doña Ximena] and [naturales] are in italics: Pidal's restorations. mis fijas naturales, 'my own daughters' (natural, 'by birth'). si f[o]re su merçed, 'if it be his grace'; f[o]re = fuere, future subjunctive of ser, its o Pidal's. Pidal's note to v. 1277: quenlas dexe, 'que me las deje', 'that he let me (have) them': quenlas = que + me + las, the me cut to its consonant and written n before l. dexe = deje, present subjunctive of dexar. sacar, 'to take out, bring away' (from Castile).

sentences.t:
Enbiaré por ellas, e vos sabed el mensage:
la mugier de mio Çid e sus fijas las iffantes
de guisa irán por ellas que a grand ondra vernán
a estas tierras estrañas que nos pudiemos ganar.”
sentences.l:
I-will-send for them, and you know-ye the message:
the wife of my Çid and his daughters the children
in manner they-will-go for them that to great honour they-will-come
to these lands foreign which we were-able to-win.”
sentences.i: I will send for them, and this is the message you are to know: for the wife of my Çid and his daughters, the children, they shall be fetched in such a manner that they will come with great honour to these foreign lands that we have been able to win.”
sentences.n: Enbiaré por ellas, 'I will send for them'. sabed, imperative 2nd pl. of saber: 'and you, know the message', i.e. here is what you are to say. mensage, 'message'. la mugier … e sus fijas las iffantes: the persons are named first and taken up again by ellas in the next line. iffantes, 'children', spelled with ff. de guisa … que, 'in such a way that'. irán por ellas, 'they will go for them', an impersonal 'they': the escort that will fetch them. a grand ondra, 'with great honour' (ondra = honra). vernán = vendrán, future of venir. estrañas, 'foreign, strange'. pudiemos, preterite 1st pl. of poder, the old -iemos ending (= pudimos).

sentences.t:
Essora dixo Minaya: “de buena voluntad.”
Pues esto an fablado, piénssanse de adobar.
sentences.l:
Then said Minaya: “of good will.”
Since this they-have spoken, they-set-themselves to make-ready.
sentences.i: Then Minaya said: “With a good will.” Now that this is spoken, they set about making ready.
sentences.n: Pidal's note to v. 1282: Essora, 'entonces', 'then' (as at v. 983). de buena voluntad, 'gladly, with a good will'. Pues, 'since, now that'. an fablado, 'they have spoken' (an = han; fablar = hablar, f- for h-). piénssanse de adobar, 'they set about making ready' (pensar de + infinitive; adobar, 'to equip, prepare').

sentences.t:
Ciento omnes le dio mio Çid a Álbar Fáñez
por servirle en la carrera [a toda su voluntad],
e mandó mill marcos de plata a San Pero levar
e que los [quinientos] diesse a don Sancho el abbat.
sentences.l:
A-hundred men to-him gave my Çid to Álbar Fáñez
for to-serve-him on the road [at all his will],
and he-ordered a-thousand marks of silver to San Pero to-take
and that the [five-hundred] he-should-give to don Sancho the abbot.
sentences.i: A hundred men my Çid gave to Álvar Fáñez to serve him on the road in all he wished; and he ordered a thousand marks of silver to be taken to San Pedro, and that he give the five hundred to Don Sancho the abbot.
sentences.n: Ciento, the full form before a noun, where the poem usually has çient (v. 1274). le … a Álbar Fáñez, the indirect object said twice, by pronoun and by name. omnes = hombres. carrera, 'road, journey'. The second half of v. 1284b, a toda su voluntad, is in italics: Pidal's restoration. mandó … levar, 'ordered … to be taken' (mandar + infinitive). San Pero = San Pedro de Cardeña, where the Çid left his wife and daughters in the care of the abbot don Sancho (v. 237 and following). [quinientos] is in italics, Pidal's restoration. los quinientos, 'the five hundred', apparently half of the thousand; Pidal gives no note here, and the line does not say what the other five hundred are for. diesse, imperfect subjunctive of dar, 'that he should give' — Minaya, presumably. abbat = abad, 'abbot'.
